newsitem.title: CHINA: China to mark Hong Kong return with Opium War film.
newsitem.headline: China to mark Hong Kong return with Opium War film.

text.p: China has finished shooting a film to mark the return of Hong Kong and has begun editing the movie about the Opium War -- the conflict that gave Britain control of the territory, state media said on Sunday.
"The movie was produced to mark the return of Hong Kong and will be released worldwide on July 1, when China resumes the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong," the official Xinhua news agency said.

The motion picture, titled "The Opium War", is directed by Xie Jin, described by Xinhua as one of China's best-known directors and renowned for creating some of China's most widely-seen, officially-sanctioned films.
Work began in May last year and the film was now being edited. It had a cast of 50,000 -- including 3,000 foreigners -- and cost 80 million yuan ($9.6 million) to produce, Xinhua said.
The 1839-1842 Opium War -- the first of a series of wars -- resulted in China ceding Hong Kong to Britain under the Treaty of Nanjing.
The treaty, which did not mention the cause of the war -- Britain's sale of opium to China -- is seen by Beijing as part of a long history of humiliating contacts with foreign powers.
